title: PUC Approves Rate Adjustment for Pennsylvania American Water
summary: Commission commends the company's efforts to bring long-term solutions to troubled water and wastewater systems across the Commonwealth MECHANICSBURG, Pa., July 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --...
body_text: Commission commends the company's efforts to bring long-term solutions to troubled water and wastewater systems across the Commonwealth MECHANICSBURG, Pa. , July 16, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- Pennsylvania American Water announced today that the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission (PUC) has ruled and approved a decision on the company's rate adjustment request. Pennsylvania American Water appreciates the PUC's thorough review of this case and remains committed to providing safe, clean, reliable, and affordable water and wastewater services to more than 2.5 million people across the Commonwealth. The PUC authorized an annual revenue increase of approximately $74.9 million to support ongoing critical infrastructure improvements, including replacing aging infrastructure, expanding PFAS treatment, and continuing efforts to eliminate lead service lines. At the same time, the decision reflects a continued focus on affordability and customer assistance. In supporting the Commission's decision, PUC Chairman Stephen M. DeFrank highlighted Pennsylvania American Water's role in helping communities served by distressed water and wastewater systems, including the company's work bringing safe drinking water to residents of Dimock, serving as receiver for systems such as Rock Spring Water Company and East Dunkard Water Authority, and investing in systems that have faced significant operational and infrastructure challenges. "The record demonstrates that Pennsylvania American Water has provided meaningful assistance to troubled water and wastewater systems through acquisitions, receiverships, and infrastructure improvements. These efforts have helped deliver safe, reliable service to customers and represent a public benefit that warrants recognition as part of the Commission's consideration of management performance," DeFrank said. The company shares Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro's focus on affordability as outlined in his recent statement of principles. While this rate case was filed before the Governor's letter, Pennsylvania American Water looks forward to engaging with the Governor's Special Counsel prior to future rate case filings to advance shared goals and ensure that Pennsylvanians continue to receive safe, clean, reliable, and affordable water and wastewater services. Pennsylvania American Water will provide further information once the order is received and its evaluation is complete, including details on how this order will affect customer bills and the implementation of the Commission's decision. Additional information about the company's rate filing and the regulatory review process is available at pennyslvaniaamwater.com/rates. About American Water American Water (NYSE: AWK) is the largest regulated water and wastewater utility company in the United States. With a history dating back to 1886 and celebrating 140 years in 2026, We Keep Life Flowing® by providing safe, clean, reliable, and affordable drinking water and wastewater services to approximately 14 million people with regulated operations in 14 states and on 18 military installations. American Water's approximately 7,000 talented professionals leverage their significant expertise and the company's national size and scale to achieve excellent outcomes for the benefit of customers, employees, investors and other stakeholders. For more information, visit amwater.com and join American Water on LinkedIn , Facebook , X and Instagram . About Pennsylvania American Water Pennsylvania American Water, a subsidiary of American Water is the largest regulated water utility in the state with approximately 1,200 dedicated employees working to provide safe, clean, reliable and affordable water and wastewater services to approximately 2.5 million people. title: News The Bancorp Bank provides SBA financing for Tallahassee assisted-living community
summary: Fintech solutions, credit solutions, and institutional banking services.
body_text: The Bancorp, Inc. (NASDAQ: TBBK) announces that its Small Business Lending team has provided an SBA 504 loan to fund construction of the Villas at Killearn Lakes, a neighborhood of assisted-living homes new to the Tallahassee community. The Bancorp is the primary financial contributor in conjunction with Florida First Capital Finance Corporation. The Villas at Killearn Lakes offers person-directed assisted living and memory care services in a unique residential setting. A groundbreaking ceremony took place May 7, 2018. The $10 million project is slated to open in early 2019. "The Bancorp is proud to support this innovative assisted-living concept and the growth it brings to the community. As an SBA lender, we are committed to helping both family-run and larger assisted-living providers grow, refinance and expand their business." Hetal Engineer, Director, SBA Sales Manager “Villas at Killearn Lakes is very pleased to be working with The Bancorp Bank and its SBA financing division,” said Dr. Chris Mulrooney, Partner and Chairman of the Board for Villas at Killearn Lakes, LLC. “Our banker, Hetal Engineer, not only grasped the vision of Villas at Killearn Lakes, but he and his team worked with us every step of the way to ensure that this project would get funded and come to fruition. The Bancorp is committed to the Villas' success and to seeing this innovative model of assisted living and memory care thrive in Tallahassee.”

title: How Better Procurement Planning Reduces Material Waste in Modular Construction
summary: See how construction procurement planning reduces material waste in modular construction, the benefits of a procurement management system, and how to build an effective plan.
body_text: Material waste in modular construction rarely comes from a single obvious mistake. It builds up quietly, through an order placed too early, a quantity rounded up "just in case," or a delivery that arrives before the factory has a place to store it. Most of that waste traces back to one place: procurement planning that was never tightly connected to actual production needs. This post looks at how effective procurement planning reduces material waste, the specific benefits it brings to modular construction, the procurement challenges that are common in this industry, and a practical approach to building a procurement plan that keeps a modular project supplied without overordering. How Effective Procurement Planning Reduces Material Waste Material waste in modular construction usually comes from a mismatch between what is ordered and what is actually needed, when it is needed, and where it needs to be. Effective construction procurement planning closes that mismatch at several points. Ordering to actual production schedules, not estimates. When purchasing is tied directly to the factory's confirmed production schedule rather than a rough project estimate, materials arrive closer to when they are consumed, reducing the excess stock that often gets damaged, misplaced, or discarded before it is used. Reducing over ordering as a buffer habit- Many teams over order out of habit, treating extra material as insurance against shortages. A structured procurement plan replaces that habit with accurate quantity takeoffs and safety stock levels calculated from real lead times, which lowers the volume of surplus material sitting unused at the end of a run. Improving storage and handling conditions- Waste is not only about ordering too much. Material that arrives too early or is stored improperly, such as panels warping in poor site conditions or components sitting exposed to weather, becomes waste just as surely as an unused surplus. Procurement planning that coordinates delivery timing with confirmed storage readiness reduces this category of loss significantly. Standardizing specifications across repeat builds- In modular construction, where the same components are often used across multiple units or projects, standardized specifications reduce the ordering errors and mismatched components that lead to scrap. Fewer variations mean fewer chances for a supplier to deliver the wrong size, grade, or finish. Better supplier coordination and lead time accuracy- When procurement planning includes clear visibility into supplier lead times and capacity, it becomes easier to place orders at the right moment rather than early, out of uncertainty about whether a supplier can deliver on short notice. Taken together, these practices shift procurement from a reactive purchasing function into a planning discipline that actively protects material, labor, and budget from waste. Key Benefits of Effective Procurement Planning in Modular Construction Beyond reducing waste directly, a well run procurement management system delivers several connected benefits specific to modular construction. Tighter alignment between factory output and site delivery- Modular builds depend on components arriving at the right stage of assembly. Strong procurement planning keeps material flow synchronized with production sequencing, reducing both idle factory time and site delays caused by missing components. Improved cost predictability- Accurate procurement planning gives cost estimators a clearer picture of material spend across a project, since quantities and timing are based on confirmed production needs rather than rough estimates padded for safety. Stronger supplier relationships and pricing leverage- Consistent, planned ordering patterns, rather than urgent last minute purchases, give suppliers more predictable demand to plan around, which often translates into better pricing and priority during periods of high demand. Reduced rework from specification errors- When procurement planning is tied closely to design and engineering data, the risk of ordering the wrong material grade, size, or finish drops, which in turn reduces the rework and scrap that come from correcting those errors mid production. Better visibility for repeat project delivery- Modular builders running similar projects across multiple sites benefit from procurement data that can be reused and refined project over project, rather than starting from scratch on every build. Lower carrying costs- Reducing surplus material also reduces the storage space, handling labor, and capital tied up in inventory that is not immediately needed, which is a meaningful cost saving on its own, separate from waste reduction. Common Procurement Challenges in Modular Construction Even with good intentions, procurement in modular construction runs into a specific set of recurring challenges. Disconnected data between design, production, and purchasing- Procurement decisions are often made from spreadsheets or documents that are not directly linked to the latest design revisions or production schedule, which leads to ordering based on outdated information. Long and variable supplier lead times-Modular construction frequently depends on specialized components and materials with longer lead times than conventional construction, and those lead times can shift with little notice, making it harder to time orders precisely. Limited visibility into factory capacity and timing-Without a clear view of when the factory is actually ready to consume a given material, procurement teams often default to ordering early, which increases the risk of waste from storage issues or spec changes made after the order is placed. Specification changes late in the process- Design changes that happen after materials have already been ordered are a major source of waste, since the original order may become unusable or require costly rework to adapt. Fragmented supplier management- Working with multiple suppliers across different material categories, often tracked in separate systems or informal communication channels, makes it difficult to get a single, reliable view of order status, pricing, and delivery commitments. Difficulty scaling procurement across multiple projects- As modular builders take on more simultaneous projects, procurement processes that worked for a single project often break down without a system built to handle overlapping demand across multiple factory runs at once. How to Create an Effective Procurement Plan for a Construction Project Building a procurement plan that actually reduces waste rather than just tracking purchases involves a few concrete steps. Start with an accurate material takeoff tied to current design data. The plan should be built from the most recent design and engineering documents, not an early estimate, since outdated takeoffs are one of the most common causes of over ordering. Map procurement timing against the production schedule. Rather than ordering based on project start date alone, align purchase orders with the specific production milestones that will consume each material, so nothing arrives significantly before it is needed. Set realistic safety stock levels based on actual lead times- Safety stock should reflect confirmed supplier lead times and their variability, not a flat percentage buffer applied out of habit. Confirm storage and handling capacity before scheduling delivery- Before finalizing a delivery date, verify that adequate, appropriate storage will be available, particularly for materials sensitive to weather or handling damage. Build in a change control process for specifications- A clear process for how design changes flow into procurement, including who approves changes and how open orders are adjusted, reduces the waste that comes from material ordered against an outdated spec. Track supplier performance over time.- Recording on time delivery rates, quality issues, and lead time accuracy by supplier helps refine future ordering decisions and identify which suppliers consistently support tighter planning. Centralize procurement data in one system. A dedicated modular construction procurement software or procurement management system that connects design, production, and purchasing data reduces the disconnects that lead to waste, and gives teams a single, current view of what has been ordered, what is in transit, and what is still needed. For builders looking to strengthen supplier coordination specifically, our guide to supplier relationship management software for construction looks at how stronger supplier data improves pricing and delivery reliability. Teams dealing with excess material sitting on site may also find our piece on moving from jobsite ordering to warehouse inventory control useful for tightening storage and handling practices. Frequently Asked Questions How is procurement planning different from purchasing in construction? Purchasing refers to the act of placing and managing individual orders. Procurement planning is the broader process of determining what to buy, when, and in what quantity, based on production schedules, design data, and supplier lead times, so that purchasing decisions are made from an accurate plan rather than ad hoc need. Can procurement planning reduce costs beyond material waste? Yes. Reduced waste is one benefit, but effective procurement planning also lowers carrying costs from excess inventory, improves supplier pricing through predictable ordering, and reduces the labor cost of managing rework caused by ordering errors. What is the biggest cause of material waste in modular construction specifically? A common cause is ordering ahead of confirmed production timing, either due to uncertainty about supplier lead times or a lack of visibility into factory scheduling, which results in materials sitting in storage long enough to be damaged, misplaced, or made obsolete by a design change. Does a procurement management system replace the need for a procurement plan? No. A procurement management system supports the plan by centralizing data and improving visibility, but the underlying plan, including takeoffs, timing, and safety stock decisions, still needs to be built around accurate project specific data. How often should a procurement plan be updated during a project? This depends on the project, but a procurement plan should be revisited whenever there is a significant design change, a shift in the production schedule, or a change in supplier lead times, rather than being treated as fixed once created at project start.

title: First Interstate and FHLB Des Moines Announce $700,000 in Grants to South Dakota Communities
summary: First Interstate and FHLB Des Moines awarded $700,000 to 34 South Dakota nonprofits through the Member Impact Fund. See recipients and how the match works.
body_text: First Interstate and Federal Home Loan Bank of Des Moines (FHLB Des Moines) will provide $700,000 in combined support to 34 nonprofit organizations across South Dakota. The total includes $200,000 from First Interstate, matched up to three times through FHLB Des Moines’ Member Impact Fund. Why It Matters These grants help organizations meet daily needs and invest in long‑term opportunity. Funds will support programs that address food security, youth development, housing stability, transportation access, workforce readiness, and other local priorities. “Partnering with FHLB Des Moines allows us to amplify our giving so more South Dakota nonprofits can move their work forward,” said Jay Mitchell, Eastern South Dakota State President. “This support helps organizations serve neighbors where it matters most.” “The Member Impact Fund match stretches each dollar further,” said Scott Reiman, Western South Dakota State President. “Together, we’re helping local partners sustain essential services and build capacity for the future.” How the Match Works Launched in 2023, the Member Impact Fund matches charitable contributions from FHLB Des Moines member institutions to eligible not‑for‑profit and government organizations. In its latest round, FHLB Des Moines announced more than $12.9 million in awards to members, distributed alongside member contributions across the Bank’s district. First Interstate’s contribution reflects our longstanding philanthropic approach. Each year, we set aside a portion of pre‑tax earnings to support community needs across our footprint. These funds back programs that develop the workforce, strengthen early childhood education, and reduce the effects of poverty. title: Procore Reviews, Pricing, and Alternatives (July 2026)
summary: Procore pricing ranges $25K-$200K+ annually. See detailed reviews, cost breakdowns, and better alternatives for mid-size GCs in July 2026.
body_text: You've probably looked at Procore alternatives because the pricing doesn't scale the way you need it to, or the onboarding timeline feels like a project in itself. Volume-based pricing means your software bill grows with your revenue, and most teams report needing three to six months before anyone's truly productive. That's a tough sell when your PM is already running procurement, managing subs, and trying to close out punch lists. We're walking through what Procore costs, where it works best, and what other options make sense for mid-size GCs who need something that works on day one. TLDR: Procore costs $10K-$60K+ annually based on your construction volume and takes 3-6 months to learn Mid-size GCs need drawing-first tools where RFIs and quality items pin to plans, not separate modules Flat-fee alternatives with unlimited users keep costs predictable as your team grows Constructable combines drawings, RFIs, financials, and daily logs in one system with under 21-day onboarding What is Procore and How Does it Work? Procore is a cloud-based construction management software built to connect field and office teams across commercial, residential, and infrastructure projects. General contractors, specialty contractors, and owners all use it to manage the full project lifecycle from a single system. The software covers a wide range of workflows: Document control and drawing management, so everyone is referencing the same set of plans RFI and submittal tracking to keep the paper trail organized and moving Daily logs and punch lists for field teams to log progress without being chained to a desk Budget tracking, invoicing, and financial management tied directly to the project Quality and safety tools to stay on top of inspections and compliance requirements Team communication and real-time reporting across all project stakeholders The idea is that everything lives in one place, so the super in the field and the PM in the office are always looking at the same information. Procore runs on a subscription model with custom pricing negotiated per company, and it has mobile apps for both iOS and Android. That said, Procore is not a light lift. Users consistently report a steep learning curve, especially for teams coming from spreadsheets or simpler tools. The system is broad by design, which means there is a lot to learn before it starts feeling natural. For larger firms with dedicated IT staff and time to train, that tradeoff can work. For mid-size teams where the PM is already handling three other jobs, it is worth knowing what you are signing up for before you commit. Why Consider Procore Alternatives? Procore is built for scale. If you run a large enterprise firm with dedicated IT staff, a training budget, and months to spare before your team gets up to speed, it can absolutely deliver. But that profile does not describe most mid-size general contractors. Here is where things get uncomfortable for a lot of teams: Pricing is tied to your annual construction volume, which means the better your business does, the more you pay. Most contractors report spending between $10,000 and $60,000+ per year, with Projul's 2026 Procore pricing breakdown citing typical annual hikes of 10-14% at renewal, and one contractor reported paying $55K annually . Proficiency takes 3 to 6 months on average, with many features going unused even after training, per G2 reviewers . Around 85% of reviewers who flagged updates said frequent changes make it hard to keep up. Users consistently flag aggressive price increases at renewal and an interface that feels overwhelming from day one. If your PM is already wearing five hats, spending half a year learning new software is not a realistic ask. Teams looking for something that works on day one, without the enterprise overhead, are right to shop around. Best Procore Alternatives in March 2026 Several solid options exist depending on your team's size, priorities, and budget. Here is how the top contenders stack up. Constructable: Best Overall Built for mid-size general contractors running $20M to $150M in volume, Constructable brings drawings, RFIs, submittals, daily logs, quality lists, financials, and bid management into one cohesive system. Flat-rate pricing with unlimited users means your bill stays predictable whether you add two people or twenty. Onboarding takes under 21 days, there is native two-way sync with QuickBooks Online and Sage Intacct, and AI-powered search works across every drawing, photo, and document on the job. No volume-based fees, no per-user charges, no surprises at renewal. Best for: Mid-size GCs tired of fragmented software stacks and enterprise complexity. Autodesk Construction Cloud Assembled through acquisitions including BIM 360, PlanGrid, and BuildingConnected, ACC offers deep BIM coordination and Revit/AutoCAD integration. It has real power for large enterprises already living in the Autodesk ecosystem, but workflows feel inconsistent across modules, migrations are expensive, and training requirements are heavy. Best for: Enterprise firms standardizing on Autodesk design tools. Fieldwire A field-first app with a fast plan viewer, task management, and punch lists. Works well for supers and foremen but lacks financial management entirely, meaning you still need separate software to run the full project. Best for: Field-only teams who handle financials elsewhere. RedTeam Budget-focused and broad in features, but widely regarded as a legacy system. Workflows feel dated, UX issues go unaddressed, and field adoption tends to be shallow. Best for: Cost-first buyers comfortable with older interfaces. Ingenious Build Built for developer portfolio oversight, not day-to-day GC workflows. Teams running active job sites often find the structure a poor fit. Best for: Owners managing multiple developments, not day-to-day GC work. Feature Comparison: Procore vs Top Alternatives Picking the right tool is easier when you can see the differences side by side. Here is how the main options compare across the features that matter most on a real job. Feature Procore Constructable Autodesk Construction Cloud Fieldwire RedTeam Ingenious Build Drawing Management Yes Yes, drawings-first with pins to RFIs and quality items Yes Yes, strong offline viewer Yes Yes RFI and Submittal Tracking Yes Yes, pinned directly to drawings Yes Basic Yes Yes Financial Management Yes Yes, QuickBooks/Sage integration Yes Limited Yes Limited Field Tools Yes Yes, with auto weather data Yes Yes, field-focused Basic Basic Unlimited Users Yes (annual contract) Yes, all plans No No, per-user Varies Varies Onboarding Timeline Weeks to months Under 21 days Weeks, often needs consultants Self-serve Self-serve Varies Pricing Model Volume-based custom quote Flat fee, no per-user charges Custom enterprise pricing $39-$89/user/month Custom quote Custom quote Mobile Offline Access Yes Yes (drawings offline) Yes Yes, strong offline Yes Yes A few things worth calling out from the table above. Procore covers a lot of ground, but that breadth comes with real tradeoffs in cost and setup time. Autodesk Construction Cloud sits in a similar tier, often requiring outside consultants just to get off the ground. Fieldwire is genuinely good for field teams but runs thin on the financial side. RedTeam and Ingenious Build offer mid-market options, though pricing and feature depth vary depending on how you configure them. Constructable sits in a different position . The flat-fee structure means your cost stays predictable whether you have five people on a project or fifty. The under-21-day onboarding timeline is a real number, not a sales claim. And the drawings-first approach reflects how most field teams actually work, starting from the plans and working outward. Why Constructable is the Best Procore Alternative Procore works well for large enterprise firms with the budget, staff, and runway to make it stick. Most mid-size GCs don't have any of those things in surplus. Constructable was built for the $20M to $150M contractor who needs everything to work without a six-month ramp. Drawings are the center of gravity here, so RFIs, quality items, and markups all live pinned to the actual plans instead of buried in separate modules. AI-powered search pulls answers across every document, photo, and drawing instantly, no clicking through nested menus to track something down. "Builders shouldn't need a software stack" is something we mean literally. One system, one login, one source of truth. Flat-fee pricing with unlimited users means adding a sub or a new PM doesn't change your invoice. True two-way sync with QuickBooks and Sage Intacct keeps financials clean without duplicate entry. Onboarding wraps in under 21 days on average. If Procore feels like more machine than you need, Constructable is worth a look. Final Thoughts on Construction Management Tools Most mid-size GCs do not need enterprise software built for Fortune 500 firms with dedicated IT departments and training budgets. What you need is something that works without eating six months of your PM's time or changing your bill every time you add someone to a project. Construction management software should connect your field and office teams without requiring a consultant to set it up or a manual to understand it. If that sounds right, talk to our team and we will walk you through how Constructable handles real jobs. FAQ When should you consider moving away from Procore? If you're spending months training your team before anyone feels comfortable, paying fees that scale with your revenue growth, or watching features change faster than your crew can keep up, it's time to look around. Most mid-size GCs find better options when the complexity and cost outweigh the actual value they're getting. What features should you look for when comparing construction management alternatives? Start with how fast your team can actually use it - if onboarding takes three months, you've already lost. Then look at pricing structure (flat-fee beats volume-based), whether drawings connect directly to RFIs and quality items, and if financials sync with your accounting software without duplicate entry. How long does it take to get your team up and running on a new system? Depends entirely on the software. Procore averages 3 to 6 months before teams feel proficient. Constructable wraps onboarding in under 21 days. Fieldwire is self-serve and faster, but you'll still need separate tools for financials. Can you switch construction management software mid-project? Yes, but timing matters. Most teams switch between projects or at natural breaks like the end of a phase. Migration gets harder if your current system doesn't export clean data, so check what you can actually take with you before you commit to leaving. Why do Procore alternatives charge less for the same features? Procore's pricing scales with your annual construction volume, so your bill climbs as your business grows. Alternatives like Constructable use flat-fee pricing with unlimited users, meaning your cost stays fixed whether you're running one project or ten. Different business model, same core workflows.

title: NS leaders recognized among rail industry's Rising Stars
body_text: Two Norfolk Southern leaders have been recognized among the railroad industry's emerging talent. Senior Director of Mechanical Operations & Support - Brian Yeager and Senior Manager of Continuous Improvement, Network Design and Optimization - Josh Williamson, have been named to Progressive Railroading's 2026 Rising Stars class, an annual recognition honoring railroad professionals under 40 who are making a significant impact on the industry. They will be featured for this award in the September issue of the magazine. Driving innovation and operational excellence The Rising Stars program recognizes professionals whose leadership, innovation, and results are helping shape the future of railroading. This year's honorees reflect NS’ commitment to developing talent and advancing solutions that improve the safety, reliability, and efficiency of the railroad. Brian Yeager: Advancing the future of freight rail inspection As Senior Director of Mechanical Operations and Support, Yeager oversees freight-car repair processes and engineering, manages wayside systems and helps ensure the effective maintenance of Norfolk Southern's freight-car fleet. He also serves as a representative on several Association of American Railroads committees. Progressive Railroading highlighted Yeager's role in helping transform freight rail inspections through advanced technologies and data-driven insights. During his career, he helped lead the deployment of innovations including NS’ 360-degree machine vision portals, wheel integrity systems, and wayside inspection corridors. title: Semrush reviews: What people say about the platform
summary: Semrush has over 6,300 online reviews across G2 and Capterra. Read a summary of the top themes seen across them.
body_text: Semrush reviews at a glance Ratings and review counts as of July 2026 Total reviews across G2 and Capterra 6,300+ G2 average rating 4.4 / 5 (4,000+ reviews) Capterra average rating 4.6 / 5 (2,300+ reviews) Most cited strengths All-in-one SEO and AI visibility platform, keyword research depth, ease of setup, client-ready reporting Semrush is a brand visibility management platform that enables marketers to audit, optimize, and quantify performance across SEO, AI search, content marketing, and paid media. Semrush has over 6,300 online reviews across G2 and Capterra . These reviews consistently point to the same thing: the benefit of one platform to replace multiple separate tools. Marketers use Semrush to research competitors, find online visibility gaps, and report results without having to stitch together data from multiple places. Here’s what people say in their online reviews. Comprehensive suite for SEO and AI visibility Customers frequently describe Semrush as an all-in-one platform for managing SEO and AI search workflows. Reviewers value being able to run keyword research, site audits, and competitor tracking without switching tools. I can tell that the team invests heavily in R&D and are always innovating." — William A., Group Director "Semrush has all the features I need to run both of my businesses. One is a brick-and-mortar medical clinic, the other an online educational website for healthcare providers. They have different needs, and Semrush combines all of them into one well functioning software application." — Eric G., Small Business Owner "Semrush has just about everything we could need as an agency offering ecommerce SEO services. We moved over from Advanced Web Ranking and carrying data over to Semrush was simple. It's intuitive with heaps of functions that make it incredibly valuable to both our business and those of our clients'. We use Semrush every single day and it fits in very well with the other tools and platforms we use. The ability to generate reports for clients helps a ton with making monthly reports easy to make and look professional. As SEO is changing, they continue to evolve the platform to help us stay at the forefront of AI's impact on SEO and AEO. It's seldom we have support needs but their customer support is very helpful! It was super easy to integrate Semrush to all of our Google, Bing, and other tools." — Greg M., eCommerce Director "I like Semrush's dashboards, which include numbers and graphs, and find the customizable date range quite handy. The setup for Semrush is seamless and I can easily integrate, copy, and paste the data into MS Office solutions like Excel and PowerPoint." — Thomas S., Principal - Product Marketing Client-ready SEO reporting Reviewers say Semrush reporting is detailed enough to present directly to clients and leadership, with visualizations that make performance and ROI easy to showcase. More importantly, it allows me to support clients better by having all the insights I need in one place. I highly recommend Semrush for business owners and agencies.” — Jose M., Business Owner "Semrush is extremely quick in giving us actionable insights into our keyword strategy and helps us identify areas for opportunity allowing us to execute an effective content marketing strategy." — Dennis M., Lead Marketing Manager B2B "I like that I can trust the reliability of Semrush's data and confidently make AEO/SEO/Content decisions based on it. I have had so many successful projects that were so in a large part due to my use of Semrush. It's an indispensable tool and I don't know where I'd be without it. In my opinion the competition does not compare." — Tom V., SEO Director "The insights are so in-depth that they create ongoing opportunities to keep creating, refining, and optimizing our content across the website, blogs, and beyond. The new AI function is really great too." — Chloe N., Digital Marketing Manager "For me, I find the organic research incredibly helpful at comparing my own website to others in the industry. Even when I stumble onto a website that as a user I like the UX of, I'll often run it through to see how their site performs to try and find takeaways I can adopt in my own UX strategy." — Cody B., Senior eCommerce Coordinator "I find Semrush to be an indispensable tool for my agency. It is used daily for comprehensive organic research, which includes keyword intelligence, position tracking, and competitive research, like PPC competitor insights and competitive gap analysis." — Fran J., CEO Unified SEO and AI visibility tracking Reviewers appreciate tracking AI visibility alongside traditional SEO data to give them one view of how their brand shows up across both traditional Google search and AI platforms like ChatGPT. "What stands out most is how Semrush is evolving beyond traditional SEO into AI visibility. The AI Visibility toolkit gives us a clearer picture of how our content is being surfaced in emerging search experiences, which is critical right now. It's helped us stay proactive instead of reactive as search behavior shifts." — Louis R., Director of Web “Great UI / UX. Love the new AI Visibility, especially the Perception and Narrative Drivers as it has allowed me to create really useful new FAQs and content that LLMs can pick up on with pre-training and inference.” — Mark C., BDM, Small Business “Semrush is extremely quick in giving us actionable insights into our keyword strategy and helps us identify areas for opportunity allowing us to execute an effective content marketing strategy. Its new AI visibility tools are also very useful in helping us develop our AEO strategy to capture AI search volume. The pricing is quite fair and is well worth it for the value it provides.” — Dennis M., Lead Marketing Manager “Semrush also gave me a different perspective on SEO, showing that it's not just about using a bunch of high-volume keywords but considering the best potential, the difficulty, and the intent. I also learned that including frequently asked questions is key in SEO and AI visibility. The initial setup of Semrush was very easy, and I find value in its ability to help reach more people and improve our visibility on Google, YouTube, and AI platforms.” — Sergio A., Copywriter and SEO Expert "I use Semrush for research, keyword and AI prompt tracking, and competitor analysis. I like its UX, which makes using the tool straightforward and effective. The initial setup was easy, making it convenient to get started." — Kyle E., SEO Consultant "I like that I have access to the raw performance data in the dashboard (as well as via the API). The MCP server for AI integration is a plus. Setting up keyword tagging allows me to monitor the effectiveness of my campaigns over time and overall, I can answer any of my search related questions using the tools that Semrush has to offer." — Michael W., Internet Technology Architect/Strategist "I use Semrush for research and AI LLM information related to my websites and SEO, and this tool is incredibly valuable. I haven't found a better bang for my buck. Semrush helps me with keyword research and finding drops and increases on my pages and websites. I like seeing the trends and finding opportunities for improvement. My favorite pieces of Semrush are the keyword tracking tools and being able to look up different URLs." — Brittany N., Marketing Manager What reviewers say about Semrush's tradeoffs While the themes above are the ones reviewers mention most often, no product receives exclusively positive feedback. The reviews also highlight a few recurring concerns. What are the most common complaints about Semrush? Across G2, Capterra, and Gartner, the most common criticisms relate to pricing, the complexity of subscriptions and add-ons, and the learning curve that comes with using a feature-rich platform. Some reviewers—particularly first-time users—say the number of available tools can feel overwhelming initially. At the same time, many reviewers describe the interface as intuitive and say they became comfortable with the platform quickly. For users who find the platform overwhelming at first, Semrush offers free resources—including Semrush Academy , the Knowledge Base , and customer support—to help shorten the learning curve. What do negative Semrush reviews say? Across G2, Capterra, and Gartner, reviewers generally agree that Semrush is a powerful platform, but some—particularly solo users and small businesses—question whether the cost is justified if they're only using a small portion of its features. Reviews suggest that perceived value depends largely on how extensively the platform is used. Businesses that rely on Semrush for keyword research, site audits, competitor analysis, reporting, and AI visibility often describe it as replacing several separate tools. Those using only one or two features are more likely to consider it expensive. For businesses with simpler needs, Semrush also offers entry-level plans, allowing users to start with a smaller subscription and expand as their requirements grow. Is Semrush pricing realistic for small businesses? Reviews suggest that perceived value depends largely on how extensively the platform is used. Businesses that rely on Semrush for research, auditing, reporting, and competitor analysis often describe it as replacing several separate tools. Those who only need one or two features are more likely to question the cost. For businesses with basic needs, Semrush offers entry-level plans that let users start with a smaller subscription and expand as their needs grow. Why do some people say Semrush isn't worth it? Reviews suggesting that Semrush “isn’t worth it” generally fall into two categories: Some reviews come from users who only use a small portion of the platform and don’t feel they’re getting enough value for the subscription cost. Other reviews come from users who found the learning curve steeper than expected before becoming comfortable with the platform. To help new users get started, Semrush provides free training through Semrush Academy , an extensive Knowledge Base , and customer support. And Enterprise teams use it to justify budgets and track global campaigns. To see what Semrush can do for you, sign up for a free seven day trial today. title: uniQure Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Company Update
summary: ~ U.S. and U.K. regulatory submissions for AMT-130 for Huntington’s disease on track as planned for the third quarter of 2026 ~ ~ Topline four-year data...
body_text: ~ U.S. and U.K. regulatory submissions for AMT-130 for Huntington’s disease on track as planned for the third quarter of 2026 ~ ~ Topline four-year data from the Phase I/II study of AMT-130 expected in September 2026 ~ ~ Reported data from the first cohort in the Phase I/IIa trial of AMT-260 for refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy showed early biological signals of therapeutic activity and a favorable safety profile ~ ~ Strengthened financial position with $259 million follow-on offering, extending cash runway into 2030 and funding the anticipated commercial launch of AMT-130 and continued pipeline investment ~ ~ uniQure to host earnings call at 8:30 a.m. ET ~ LEXINGTON, Mass. and AMSTERDAM, July 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- uniQure N.V. (NASDAQ: QURE), a leading gene therapy company advancing transformative therapies for patients with severe medical needs, today reported its financial results for the second quarter of 2026 and highlighted recent progress across its business. “This has been a defining quarter – not just for uniQure, but for the Huntington's disease community,” said Matthew Kapusta, chief executive officer at uniQure . “Following a productive Type B meeting with the FDA, we remain on track to submit our BLA for AMT-130 in the third quarter — a milestone that reflects years of rigorous science, disciplined execution, and an unwavering commitment to the patients and families living with this devastating disease. With four-year data expected in September and the U.K. regulatory activities progressing as planned, we enter the second half of 2026 with real momentum and a clear line of sight to potentially bringing this therapy to the people who need it.” “Beyond AMT-130, we continue to execute across our broader pipeline,” Mr. Kapusta continued. “With a strong balance sheet, we believe we are well-positioned for what will be a transformative period for uniQure and the patients we serve.” Recent Company Developments and Updates Advancing AMT-130 for the treatment of Huntington’s disease In June 2026, the Company held a Type B meeting with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). Official meeting minutes received in July 2026 confirmed that the FDA and the Company reached alignment that a Biologics License Application (BLA) submission under the accelerated approval pathway for AMT-130, based on the existing clinical data, is reasonable. In addition, the FDA seeks to align on the confirmatory study design prior to the BLA submission, including consideration of a randomized standard-of-care control design instead of a sham procedure. The FDA also stated that, in accordance with the FDA’s draft public guidance for accelerated approvals, the confirmatory study should be feasible to conduct within a reasonable timeline and be well underway, and potentially fully enrolled, at the time of accelerated approval. Discussions with the FDA to align on the confirmatory study design and analysis are underway and the Company expects to submit a BLA in the third quarter of 2026. The Company plans to initiate the confirmatory study as expeditiously as possible after aligning with the FDA on the trial design. In September 2026, the Company plans to present data from its ongoing Phase I/II studies of AMT-130. The update is expected to include follow-up data on all patients treated with AMT-130 in the first two cohorts, including four years of follow-up on 24 patients (12 patients at the high-dose and 12 patients at the low dose). In March 2026, the Company held a successful pre-submission meeting with the United Kingdom’s (U.K.) Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) and the regulatory submission is progressing as planned for the third quarter of 2026. Continued clinical progress in pipeline programs AMT-260 for the treatment of refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (MTLE) In June 2026, the Company announced preliminary six-month follow-up data on the first, low dose cohort of six patients in the ongoing Phase I/IIa study. As of the May 29, 2026 data cutoff date, three of six patients in the first, low-dose cohort achieved meaningful reductions in disabling seizures during months four through six of follow-up, ranging from a 79% to 100% decline from baseline. The remaining three patients in the low-dose cohort experienced variable changes in disabling seizures during months four through six of follow-up, ranging from a 33% decrease to a 36% increase compared to baseline. As of the June 19, 2026 presentation date, there were no Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) related to AMT-260 or the surgical procedure reported. All reported adverse events in the low dose cohort were classified as mild or moderate in severity, with the most common adverse event being headache (N=2). No immunosuppression was required. The Company expects to complete enrollment in the second dose cohort in the Phase I/IIa study in the third quarter of 2026. The Company expects to present updated results from the Phase I/IIa study in the first half of 2027. AMT-191 for the treatment of Fabry disease In June 2026, the Company presented new data from the Phase I/II study of AMT-191 in Fabry disease. The data, with a cutoff date of March 15, 2026, included patient follow-up ranging from three months to more than 18 months and consisted of the following: Dose-dependent elevations were observed across 11 patients in three dose levels with α-Gal A activity ranging from 1- to 16.2-fold above mean normal range (1.38-8.66 nmol; mean normal of 3.57 nmol) at the lowest dose, 14.5- to 229.6-fold at the mid dose, and 58.7- to 143.6-fold at the highest dose. Plasma lyso-Gb3 levels remained stable post-dose across all cohorts, regardless of enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) status. All 11 dosed patients were withdrawn from ERT. AMT-191 continued to show a manageable safety profile at all dose levels. No SAEs related to AMT-191 were observed at the low and mid doses. No additional SAEs were observed at the high dose beyond those previously reported in September 2025 in two patients. Per protocol, additional dosing in the mid- and high-dose cohorts remains paused, pending further evaluation of asymptomatic liver enzyme elevations reported in two patients from the mid-dose cohort, which were confirmed as dose-limiting toxicities. These elevations resolved as of the end of May 2026 following a course of immunosuppression as per the study protocol. Focused execution and strong financial position In June 2026, the Company closed an upsized underwritten public offering of 5,686,813 ordinary shares at a public offering price of $45.50 per share, including the full exercise of the underwriters’ option to purchase additional shares. The aggregate gross proceeds to uniQure from the offering, before deducting the underwriting discounts and commissions and offering expenses payable by uniQure, were $259 million. As of June 30, 2026, the Company had cash, cash equivalents and current investment securities of $810.3 million. The Company expects that these resources will be sufficient to fund projected operating expenses into 2030. Financial Highlights Cash Position: As of June 30, 2026, the Company held $810.3 million in cash, cash equivalents and current investment securities, compared to $622.5 million as of December 31, 2025. The Company expects that these resources will be sufficient to fund our projected operating expenses into 2030. Revenues: Revenue for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $5.8 million, compared to $5.3 million in the same period in 2025. The increase of $0.5 million is due to an increase in license revenue, compared to the prior period. R&D Expenses: Research and development expenses were $34.0 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $35.4 million during the same period in 2025. The $1.4 million decrease was driven by a $3.2 million decrease in other research and development expenses, partially offset by a $1.8 million increase in direct research and development expenses. The decrease in other research and development expenses primarily reflected a $1.5 million decrease in facility expenses, a $1.3 million decrease in employee and contractor-related expenses, including share-based compensation, and a $1.0 million decrease in the fair value of contingent consideration, partially offset by a $0.6 million increase in information technology costs. The increase in direct research and development expenses reflected higher spend on the AMT-260, AMT-162 and AMT-191 programs, partially offset by lower spend on AMT-130, compared to the prior period. SG&A Expenses: Selling, general and administrative expenses were $17.4 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $13.5 million during the same period in 2025. The $3.9 million increase was primarily related to a $4.3 million increase in employee and contractor-related expenses, including share-based compensation, mainly as a result of a higher number of employees recruited in the second half of 2025 to support the potential commercial launches of AMT-130, a $0.7 million increase in intellectual property fees, and a $0.7 million increase in information technology costs and other expenses. This was partially offset by a $1.8 million decrease in professional fees, primarily as a result of lower costs incurred in support of the potential commercial launches of AMT-130, compared to the prior period. Other Expense: Other expense increased to $8.0 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026 from $2.2 million during the same period in 2025, primarily due to a $6.0 million increase in costs associated with the supply of HEMGENIX® to CSL Behring. Other non-Operating Items, net: Other non-operating items, net was an expense of $27.0 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to a gain of $6.6 million during the same period in 2025. The $33.6 million increase in net non-operating expense was primarily related to a $20.4 million unfavorable change in net foreign currency, from an $18.6 million gain to a $1.7 million loss, and a $16.0 million loss resulting from changes in the fair value of the liability related to pre-funded warrants, compared to nil in the prior period. This was partially offset by a $1.5 million increase in interest income and a $1.2 million decrease in interest expense, compared to the prior period. Net loss: The net loss for the three months ending June 30, 2026, was $81.1 million, or $1.22 basic and diluted loss per ordinary share, compared to a $37.7 million net loss for the comparative period in 2025, or $0.69 basic and diluted loss per ordinary share. Upcoming investor events: 2026 Biotech Summer Summit, August 10 -12 – Newport, RI Investor Conference Call and Webcast Information uniQure management will host an investor conference call and webcast today, Wednesday, July 29th at 8:30 a.m. ET. The event will be webcast under the Events & Presentations section of uniQure’s website at https://www.uniqure.com/investors-media/events-presentations , and following the event a replay will be archived for 90 days. Analysts wishing to participate in the question and answer session should access the live call by dialing (646) 307-1963 or toll-free (800) 715-9871 and entering conference ID 5075555. If you are joining the conference call, please join 15 minutes before the start time. The approvals of uniQure’s gene therapy for hemophilia B – an historic achievement based on more than a decade of research and clinical development – represent a major milestone in the field of genomic medicine and ushers in a new treatment approach for patients living with hemophilia. uniQure is now advancing a pipeline of proprietary gene therapies for the treatment of patients with Huntington's disease, refractory temporal lobe epilepsy, Fabry disease, and other severe diseases. www.uniQure.com uniQure Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements. title: Ocean Freight Impacts: Hormuz Status Update and Analysis
summary: Is the Strait open or closed? The US and Iran signed a Memorandum of Understanding in mid-June through which they agreed in principle to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The US ended its blockade soon after and Iran committed to allowing vessels to pass – toll free – during the 60-day period set to negotiate […]
body_text: Is the Strait open or closed? The US and Iran signed a Memorandum of Understanding in mid-June through which they agreed in principle to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The US ended its blockade soon after and Iran committed to allowing vessels to pass – toll free – during the 60-day period set to negotiate a final peace agreement. So the strait has technically been reopened since June. But even if there were complete calm in the waterway – which has not been the case – estimations are that it will take weeks to months for traffic to rebound to pre-war levels. The recovery will take time because Iranian mines, which could take months to remove and demining may not start until a final deal is reached, have made the main central passage unpassable. As such, passing vessels are limited to two narrow lanes, one in the north of the strait along the Iranian coast and one in the south along Oman. Towards the end of June the UN’s International Maritime Organization began implementing an organized evacuation plan aimed at orchestrating vessel exits out of the Persian Gulf along the southern route. Iran vying for long term control The UN’s Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) considers the Strait of Hormuz an international strait, and therefore requires neighboring countries to allow vessels to pass unimpeded. Iran however never ratified the UNCLOS, and argues that under international law it has the right to control traffic under some circumstances (though probably not for neutral merchant vessels). Authorized route being promoted by Iran’s Persian Gulf Authority. Source: Persian Gulf Authority In any case, Iran has advised all vessels in the region to transit only via the northern lane and in coordination with the Strait Authority it has set up. Periodic Iranian attacks on vessels using other lanes, as well as on neighboring countries, probably aimed at forcing traffic through its channel – followed by US retaliations – have further limited the speed of traffic recovery through multiple stops and starts. The IMO officially paused its evacuation effort just days after it started, in response to Iranian threats. Nonetheless, traffic through the Strait overall has increased compared to before the ceasefire, but has fluctuated and is still well below pre-war levels. Impact on freight markets Freight operations Operationally, the strait’s closure did not disrupt the overall container market, but did significantly impede container traffic in and out of the Gulf states. The renewed traffic comprises mostly tankers, though some container vessels have exited the Gulf since the ceasefire began while very few have entered. For now, shippers trying to get containers into (or out of) the Gulf states continue to rely on alternative , still accessible ports in the UAE, Oman and Saudi Arabia and then, sometimes very lengthy, road transport. Shipments via these alternatives have faced long delays and steep pricetags, and the fact that volumes haven’t dropped on these lanes show that for Gulf container traffic there has not been much of a recovery yet. Even once the situation is more stable, container carriers are likely to activate mostly feeder services instead of long haul port calls to the Gulf until confidence returns to the lane. Freight rates Though the broader container market was spared operational disruptions, the Strait of Hormuz closure did have a significant impact on the overall market by way of rising fuel costs. Emergency Fuel Surcharges led to transpacific container rates climbing $1,000/FEU and 50% over the first two months of the war. Sharp Bunker Adjustment Factor hikes set for July 1st, as well as Q3 manufacturer price increases, are probably key factors to the early surge of peak season demand for both transpacific and Asia – Europe lanes , which have pushed container rates up by $3,000 – $4,000/FEU on these trades since the end of May. Oil prices have already eased back to pre-war levels, with the speed of the crude rebound is taking many experts by surprise and even leading to concerns of oversupply. Bunker fuel prices have eased significantly as well , but still remain about 30% higher than pre-war levels. Refined petroleum products are likely to take a little longer to normalize, as they depend on a crude recovery first, but oil market behavior makes it likely that bunker prices are on their way back to normal. Join 70,000+ Supply Chain Experts Who Never Miss an Issue! Start your week with the industry insights others miss. " * " indicates required fields The bottom line That oil prices are stabilizing even before Strait of Hormuz traffic has returned to normal is a good sign that freight rates – once peak season demand subsides – will also face downward pressure from normalizing bunker prices, and could return closer to pre-war levels before the end of the year. A recovery to normal container flows (and freight rates) for the Gulf states will likely take much longer, and there are reports that countries in the region are planning on investing in better infrastructure for those alternative routes as they look to the future.
